title: What happens after extreme funding rates? 789 days of data
snippet:
We measured forward returns after extreme funding percentiles on BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, XRP and DOGE: 789 days, three venues. Two popular beliefs fail the test.

Two beliefs circulate about perpetual funding, and they point in opposite directions. The first: when funding is extremely high, longs are crowded and a top is near — fade it. The second: when funding is deeply negative, shorts are crowded and a squeeze is coming — buy it.

Both sound like microstructure. Both are testable. We ran them against every hour of our cross-venue funding history — 789 days, from May 15, 2024 to July 13, 2026, across BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, XRP and DOGE — and measured what price actually did in the next 4, 24 and 72 hours.
...
- After BTC funding entered its top decile (≥90th percentile of its own 2-year history), the median 72-hour forward return was −1.18%, with only 40.5% of episodes resolving up (n = 37 non-overlapping episodes). On BTC, stretched funding did precede weakness.
- The same condition on ETH, BNB, XRP and DOGE produced positive median 72-hour returns of +0.95%, +1.10%, +1.73% and +0.72%, with hit rates of 53–57%. On most alts, extreme funding preceded more upside, not a top.
- Deeply negative funding (≤10th percentile) predicted nothing on any of the six assets: median 72-hour forward returns between −0.48% and +0.62%, hit rates between 46.6% and 54.1%. The "negative funding = short squeeze" trade is a coin flip in this sample.
...

# Delta-Neutral Funding Rate Carry — Falsification Study

Part of a public portfolio of pre-registered falsification studies on
retail-accessible crypto trading signals. See prior work:
`friday-monday-fade-falsification`, `volatility-breakout-falsification`,
`turtle-soup-smt-falsification`, `retail-crypto-alpha`.

**Status: Falsified.** Full methodology locked in `PREREGISTRATION.md`
before any data was collected. Split date locked before any result was
computed (`data/SPLIT_DATE.txt`, `2023-02-06`).
...
The base hypothesis — that a delta-neutral position (long spot / short
perp, or the inverse) initiated when funding rate exceeds a trailing
percentile threshold produces a net-of-cost positive return — is
**falsified** across all three pre-registered assets (BTC, ETH, SOL) and
all pre-registered variants (V1 static percentile, V2 rolling z-score, V3
rebalanced/non-rebalanced).

Out-of-sample mean net return per trade is negative in every single
symbol x variant combination tested, with no exceptions:

| Symbol | Variant | OOS mean net return | OOS trades |
|---------|---------|---------------------|------------|
| BTCUSDT | V1 | -0.428% | 119 |
| BTCUSDT | V2 | -0.433% | 150 |
| ETHUSDT | V1 | -0.425% | 131 |
| ETHUSDT | V2 | -0.428% | 139 |
| SOLUSDT | V1 | -0.417% | 189 |
| SOLUSDT | V2 | -0.396% | 128 |

# Spot money-flow signals for BTCUSDT perpetuals — a falsification-first research program
...
Two pre-registered studies test whether a spot Money Flow Index (MFI) signal, alone or combined with
perp funding, predicts Binance USDⓈ-M BTCUSDT perpetual returns. Both were closed honestly: the base
study is `FALSIFIED`, and its follow-up (Variant A) is `INCONCLUSIVE`, weight of evidence leaning
`FALSIFIED`. Nothing here was tuned toward a flattering result — a clean negative is the deliverable.
...
**Base study — raw spot-MFI momentum: `FALSIFIED`.**
The factor's honest (non-overlapping) Information Coefficient was statistically indistinguishable from
zero (p ≈ 0.30–0.46) before any strategy was built. Optimising anyway: an in-sample parameter plateau
peaked at Sharpe 1.07 (not a spike — 3×3 neighbourhood retained 85% of peak Sharpe), but the embargoed
walk-forward out-of-sample Sharpe collapsed to **0.29**, below buy-and-hold spot (0.46) and below the
pre-registered 0.5 floor. 0 of 42 grid configs survived Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction. 2 of the 7
pre-registered gates passed (plateau, cost-robustness); the other 5 — including both out-of-sample
significance gates — failed.

title: Can Funding Rate Predict Price Change? | Presto Research
snippet:
- We explore the potential of using funding rates in perpetual futures contracts to predict future price changes.
- Funding rate changes initially account for 12.5% of the variation in price changes over a 7-day period.
- The predictive power diminishes for subsequent periods, indicating limited reliability for single asset predictions.
- Funding rate data may be more useful when applied cross-sectionally across multiple assets.
- A statistical arbitrage alpha using funding rate data shows favorable performance metrics but requires refinement to reduce its turnover.
...
The cryptocurrency market, characterized by its volatility and rapid price fluctuations, has seen the rise of various financial instruments designed to capitalize on these dynamics. Among these, perpetual futures contracts have gained significant traction, allowing traders to speculate on the future prices of digital assets without an expiration date. Central to the functioning of these contracts is the funding rate—a periodic payment mechanism intended to keep the perpetual futures price in line with the underlying spot price. We address the intriguing question: Can the funding rate of perpetual futures be used to predict future price changes?

title: Extreme Perpetual Futures Funding and Subsequent Bitcoin Returns: Intraday Evidence from Binance
snippet:
# Extreme Perpetual Futures Funding and Subsequent Bitcoin Returns: Intraday Evidence from Binance
...
Perpetual futures funding rates are central to cryptocurrency derivatives markets because they help anchor perpetual-contract prices to spot prices while simultaneously reflecting the state of the derivatives market. This study examines whether historically extreme Bitcoin perpetual-futures funding rates contain information about subsequent Bitcoin spot returns. Binance BTCUSDT perpetual funding observations from 10 September 2019 to 10 August 2026 are aligned with Binance BTCUSDT spot prices sampled at 15-minute frequency. Extreme funding is classified ex ante using the current funding rate's mid-rank percentile within the preceding 180-day distribution, with the lower and upper deciles defining extreme negative and extreme positive states. Bitcoin spot returns are measured over 15-minute, one-hour, four-hour, eight-hour and 24-hour post-settlement horizons. Parametric, non-parametric and directional tests are supplemented by heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation consistent regressions controlling for the four-hour price movement preceding settlement. The main result is concentrated in the negative tail: extreme negative funding is followed by an average 24-hour Bitcoin return of 0.506%, significant under t, Wilcoxon and directional-frequency tests and robust to false-discovery-rate adjustment.
